speaker_role: independent educational consultant (Lee Educational Consulting, appears to work with international/Hong Kong-based applicants)
commercial_incentive: yes - video is explicitly made for the consultant's own students as a prep step before a one-on-one activity-list review
key_insights: The activities list should be completed before brainstorming the personal statement, since it captures granular details that would otherwise eat up essay word count
Descriptions (150 characters) should use concise action verbs (raised, organized, oversaw) describing the student's personal role, not just the organization's general activities
Organization and leadership-position names should be spelled out in full with no abbreviations, since US admissions officers won't know local/school-specific acronyms
After filling in all 10 activity slots, students must prioritize and reorder them, factoring in relevance to intended major, duration/commitment, and leadership level
University-affiliated summer programs should be entered under the Common App's Education section (colleges attended), not listed as an activity, to avoid wasting activity slots
A demonstrated example shows combining multiple roles/accomplishments into a single tightly-edited bullet-style description to maximize the limited character count
specific_numbers_or_facts: Common App activities section allows a maximum of 10 entries, per the presenter
Activity description field is capped at roughly 150 characters, per the presenter
notable_or_distinctive: Live screen-recorded walkthrough of the actual Common App activities interface, including a real (redacted) student example and a step-by-step mock entry built live for an 'architecture club' activity.
reliability_notes: Practical, hands-on demo rather than abstract advice, but presented informally with some rambling and self-correction; specific character/field limits should be verified against the current Common App since the platform can change over time (video is 5 years old).
